newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil house to vote civil service bill amendments.
newsitem.headline: Brazil house to vote civil service bill amendments.

text.p: Brazil's lower house was expected to resume voting Tuesday afternoon on proposed amendments to a bill reforming the civil service, government leaders said.
The government's chief whip Benito Gama told reporters the government aimed to restart the balloting on the amendments after 1600 local/1500 EDT/1900 GMT Tuesday and complete it on Wednesday.
"We intend to complete the voting Wednesday because there's a holiday next week and it will be difficult to get a quorum," Gama said.
Regarded as a central plank of the government's efforts to rein in public spending, the civil service reforms were approved in a first round ballot in the lower house last month.

They then became bogged down in voting on amendments. The government was dealt a stunning blow when it failed to kill one amendment which effectively removed from the bill one of its main tenets, the right to sack temporary workers.
Among the amendments still to be voted on are some of the most controversial, including one that refers to job guarantees and another on maximum salary levels for civil servants.
